rows.question: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.restated: What kinds of old photos do users struggle to retrieve?
rows.text:
People struggle with old photos they only vaguely remember. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] The stories cover three kinds. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]
- Among memories like people, trips, or events, 13 of 48 stories (27%) say the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:sentimental]]
- Where the post does not say why the photo was kept, 15 of 46 stories (33%) say the same — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:unclear]]
- For receipts, documents, or notes, 3 of 21 stories say the search did not understand what they typed. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:utility]]
One post simply asks for an “old screenshot” — “I need old screenshot picc” [[story|313e52d4d7afb19798f4bb12be3491ecf5803425:0]].
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a breakdown of other things that went wrong for each kind?*

rows.question: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.restated: What information do people actually remember about a photo?
rows.gap: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on what they actually remember about the photo to rely on it
rows.text:
These stories can’t reliably tell what people actually remember about a photo, because two AI readers agreed too rarely on it. [[analysis_reliability|q:2.1]][[analysis_method_flags|no_gold_standard]]  
People most often remembered what was in the photo, like the main subject. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:main_subject@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:what:core]]  
Some remembered when it was taken, such as the year. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=when:year@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:when:core]]  
Others recalled who was in it, like people present. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=who:people_present@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_derived|cue_remembered:who:core]]  
One person wrote they searched the words in a poster and found it — “I searched the words on the posters” [[story|90c8b5f8d8913d764335d981d06c5dc02200c937:0]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.1=what:visible_text@photo_class:_all]]  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a quick summary by place and event too?*

rows.question: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.restated: What information have people forgotten about the photo they want?
rows.text:
People most often forgot when the photo was taken. [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:when:core]] They also forgot the date or year. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=date_or_year@photo_class:_all]] Some forgot where it was taken, including the exact place or venue name. [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:where:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=exact_place_or_venue_name@photo_class:_all]] A few forgot where it came from or whether it was a photo, video or screenshot. [[analysis_derived|cue_forgotten:source:core]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=photo_video_or_screenshot@photo_class:_all]] One story even forgot which app or account held it. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:2.4=which_app_or_account@photo_class:_all]] One post shows this feeling: “I had totally forgotten” [[story|b526179286c2b3c9db1c198db44e50543ed2f275:0]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want examples of how people still found the photo despite this?*

rows.question: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.restated: How do users formulate searches when their memory is incomplete?
rows.text:
People often type a simple thing they remember, like an object or action. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]][[story|790de55c9d650cb50647f97841544a0c5b1b7275:0]] Many stories say the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos, in 31 of 115 stories (27%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]] Some do find photos this way: “I just search Google Photos for ‘bicycle’, and find it” [[story|790de55c9d650cb50647f97841544a0c5b1b7275:0]]. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] Others try words from text in the photo. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]][[story|90c8b5f8d8913d764335d981d06c5dc02200c937:0]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want examples by kind of detail people typed?*

rows.question: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.restated: Does Google Photos fail to understand the clues people give it?
rows.text:
Yes, often. In 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that the search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] Some people said things like “dog with black hair” got no results, or “dog” showed “hot-dog”. [[story|c06874c9c9acadf8038072c41b2d0d2c08c2bc10:0]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]] Still, in 38 of 115 stories (33%), nothing went wrong — they found the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]] One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to look at what goes wrong when people never use the search box?*

rows.question: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.restated: What is Google Photos' annual revenue?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text: The stories do not include financial or revenue data for Google Photos or Alphabet/Google, so they cannot answer this. These are public posts about trying to find a photo, not company accounts or earnings reports. To answer this, we would need audited financial statements or official segment disclosures from Alphabet that break out Google Photos revenue.

rows.question: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.restated: How many people use Ask Photos every month?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text:
These are public posts about trying to find a photo, so they cannot tell us how many people use Ask Photos every month.  
They cannot show a rate of success or failure, and they cannot give a count of users.  
Data from product analytics or a representative survey would be needed to answer this.

rows.question: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories?
rows.restated: What is the success rate for searches from vague memories?
rows.gap: these are public stories, not usage data: no rate of success or failure, and no count of users, can be produced from them
rows.text:
These are public posts about trying to find a photo, so they cannot give a success rate for searches from vague memories. They also cannot tell how many users tried or how often they succeeded or failed. Data from product logs or a representative user study would be needed to answer this.

*Would you like me to explain what kind of study could estimate that rate?*

rows.question: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.restated: Do Android users struggle to find photos more than iPhone users?
rows.gap: the posts do not reliably say which phone people use, so there is no Android vs iPhone split
rows.draft:
A comparison of Android vs iPhone is not possible from these stories — they are public posts without reliable device or platform labels, so no valid split can be made. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

What we can say is where the stories came from. 3,000 posts were app‑store reviews: 2,500 from the App Store and 2,000 from Google Play. [[analysis_sources|appstore]][[analysis_sources|play]]
Most posts were not from app stores at all: 18,662 from YouTube comments and 5,042 from X (Twitter). [[analysis_sources|youtube]][[analysis_sources|x]]
One person said “IOS Photos does it on specific numbers” [[story|ac7cfeda39451a237d2ad146b43c59993c4a9c0a:0]], but posts cannot show device splits. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a breakdown of what people remembered when they searched?*
rows.text:
The stories cannot tell you all of this: the posts do not reliably say which phone people use, so there is no Android vs iPhone split. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|c6af9dfa5d9eb9733869f6f5824fc1c29a4acbae:0]]

Every figure counts stories people chose to post in public. It is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to ask it more narrowly?*

rows.question: Has search got worse since Ask Photos launched?
rows.restated: Has search got worse since Ask Photos launched?
rows.gap: the stories were not compared across time, so there is no before-and-after
rows.text:
We cannot tell if search got worse after Ask Photos launched, because the stories were not compared across time. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]  
We can say what went wrong for people who only vaguely remembered the photo. [[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
In 31 of 115 stories (27%), the search did not understand what they typed, or it showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
In 9 of 115 stories (8%), the photo was in the results but hard to spot among similar ones. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=6@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_funnel|stories:core]]  
One person said they could not find a picture of a tick: “I can’t find it.” [[story|13c83c4d63cabfee54ac7ee7f9faf8fe91157833:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a breakdown of these stories by what people tried first?*

rows.question: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.restated: Is Apple Photos search better than Google Photos search at finding old photos?
rows.gap: the stories do not compare how well other photo apps search
rows.text:
These stories cannot compare Apple Photos with Google Photos, so they cannot say which search is better. [[analysis_method_flags|missing_cuts]]

People often say the first problem was that search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos — 31 of 115 stories (27%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]
Some found the photo with no trouble — 38 of 115 stories (33%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]
One person said it was “trivial to do in Google Photos” to find a years‑old photo. [[story|b7113e3689e0674b9cd8b089fb3bcd093e40d3eb:0]]
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Would you like the same split for when the photo was already gone?*

rows.question: How deep do people scroll through search results before deciding?
rows.restated: How far down search-results lists did people scroll before deciding (how deep did they scroll)?
rows.gap: few public posts say anything about how far down the results they went — 2 of 115 stories do — so it is left for interviews with real users
rows.text:
Only two stories say how far people went: one says they scrolled a few times, and one says they went all the way down. [[analysis_coverage|6.6]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=a_few_scrolls@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=exhaustive@photo_class:_all]] In stories about photos kept as memories, 1 of 48 stories (2%) says a few scrolls — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=a_few_scrolls@photo_class:sentimental]] In stories where the post does not say why the photo was kept, 1 of 46 stories (2%) says all the way down — a small group, so only a rough guide. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:6.6=exhaustive@photo_class:unclear]] One person wrote they “had to scroll way too far back” [[story|bc5c550e736b8cf3ff06a1ac0de6b70da0f425ec:0]].

One limit is that few public posts say how far down the results they went — 2 of 115 stories — so it is left for interviews with real users. [[analysis_method_flags|interview_register]][[analysis_coverage|6.6]]

*Do you want the same figures split by why people kept the photo?*

rows.question: How often does a wrong year act as a hard filter that hides the photo?
rows.restated: How often does a wrong year act as a hard filter that hides the photo?
rows.gap: few public posts say anything about whether the system discarded the photo because one detail was wrong — 22 of 290 stories do — so it is left for interviews with real users
rows.text:
Only a few public posts say whether one wrong detail made the system drop the photo, so interviews with real users are needed. [[analysis_coverage|5.3]][[analysis_method_flags|interview_register]]  
In 1 of 115 stories (1%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, adding more words made the photo disappear. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.3=and_logic_shrinks_recall@photo_class:_all]]  
In 2 of 115 stories (2%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, a small mistake in a detail did not matter. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:5.3=soft_ok@photo_class:_all]]  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

"it says no results" [[story|c06874c9c9acadf8038072c41b2d0d2c08c2bc10:0]]

*Want to compare this with wrong place or person details?*

rows.question: How many attempts do people make before they give up?
rows.restated: How many attempts do people make before they give up searching for a photo?
rows.gap: two AI readers went through the stories separately and agreed too rarely on how long they kept trying to rely on it
rows.text:
These stories cannot tell how many attempts people make before they give up, because two AI readers agreed too rarely on how long they kept trying. [[analysis_method_flags|low_reliability_fields]]  
Some posts do say how long they kept trying. [[analysis_coverage|8.1]]  
In 21 of 115 stories (18%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, they made one try. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=one_attempt@photo_class:_all]]  
In 6 of 115 stories (5%), they tried a few times over some minutes. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=few_attempts_minutes@photo_class:_all]]  
In 3 of 115 stories (3%), they kept at it for an hour or more. [[analysis_crosstab|core.q:8.1=hour_or_more@photo_class:_all]]  
“No matter how many times I look back at the photos, I can't find” [[story|3f6c7b626f52b658b0c519881ff8cb6967208570:0]].  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a breakdown by why the photo was kept?*

rows.question: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
rows.restated: Why does Ask Photos fail most often?
rows.text:
Most often, the search did not understand what people typed, or it showed the wrong photos: 31 of 115 stories (27%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]][[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]
Next, the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else: 20 of 115 stories (17%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]]
Some people never used the search box and just scrolled: 9 of 115 stories (8%). [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=3@photo_class:_all]]
One person asked, “Mera photo delete ho gaya hai… kaise layge wapas” [[story|42529531479d94c63703412b94c9139531d45bf9:0]]
One limit is that these are public posts, not a share of users or searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want a plain summary you can share with your team?*

rows.question: Since most failures happen because the photo was deleted, what should Google fix first?
rows.restated: Since most failures happen because the photo was deleted, what should Google fix first?
withheld: unverifiable quote: text search … and be disappointed.
rows.draft:
Fix search so it understands simple cues first. [[analysis_opportunity|stage5]][[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]  
In 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a photo the person only vaguely remembered, the first thing that went wrong was that search did not understand what they typed, or showed the wrong photos. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]  
Apply AI to interpret short, vague words, connect them to people, places, and time, and index concepts and objects better. [[analysis_synthesis|recommendation:intelligence_needed]]  
One post says “text search … and be disappointed.” [[analysis_synthesis|recommendation:chain:evidence]][[story|beebc7898400af1a0cc9f1ea6c04d016e3940312:0]]  
One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Would you like a brief example of how better cue understanding could work?*
rows.text:
- The problem — search did not understand or match what they typed — comes up in 31 of 115 stories (27%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 30 people. It is the one problem with enough stories to rank. [[analysis_opportunity|stage5]]
- The problem — the photo was gone before anyone searched — deleted, never backed up, elsewhere — comes up in 20 of 115 stories (17%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 20 people. Better search could not fix it. [[analysis_opportunity|stage0]]
- The problem — they never searched — scrolled the timeline or didn't know search could help — comes up in 9 of 115 stories (8%) about a vaguely remembered photo, from 9 people. Too few stories to rank it. [[analysis_opportunity|stage3]]
- One of the posts this rests on, to read in full [[story|beebc7898400af1a0cc9f1ea6c04d016e3940312:0]]

Every figure counts stories people chose to post in public. It is not a success rate, and not a share of Google Photos users or of searches. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

*Want to ask it more narrowly?*

rows.question: What share of utility-photo stories end with the person giving up?
rows.restated: What share of practical-photo stories end with the person giving up?
rows.gap: only 21 stories are about photos kept for the information in them (receipts, documents, notes) — too few (under 30) for a percentage, so only counts are given
rows.text:
These stories cannot tell a share, because only 21 stories are about photos kept for the information in them — too few (under 30) for a percentage, so only counts are given. [[analysis_method_flags|thin_core]]

Among these utility-photo stories, 8 of 21 say the photo was already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:utility]]
6 of 21 say nothing went wrong — they found the photo. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=9@photo_class:utility]]
4 of 21 say they could not remember enough about the photo to search for it. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=2@photo_class:utility]]
One post says the search returned “way too many images” when looking for a receipt — “way too many images of my shop.” [[story|0ef3821f2d59998617a4b53f428fd49c9a22d2ff:0]]

One limit is that these are public posts. [[analysis_method_flags|proxy_not_success_rate]]

rows.question: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.restated: What happens when people search for a pet photo and cannot find it?
rows.text:
Most often, the search misunderstands the words or shows the wrong photos, so people still cannot find the pet shot. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=5@photo_class:_all]]  
Sometimes the photo is already gone — deleted, never backed up, or kept somewhere else. [[analysis_crosstab|core.primary_stage=0@photo_class:_all]]
